{{Short description|French physicist (born 1942)}}
'''Alain Rouet''' (born 1942 in France) is a French [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]], entrepreneur, poet, and novelist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.alain-rouet.com/|title=Alain Rouet (homepage); alain-rouet.com}}</ref>

==Education and career==
At the [[École Centrale Paris|École Centrale des Arts et Manufactures]], Rouet graduated in 1969 with an engineering degree and in 1974 with a [[doctorate]] in theoretical physics. He worked as a postdoc for the academic year 1975–1976 at the [[Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics]] (MPA) in [[Munich]] and from 1976 to 1978 at [[CERN]]. From 1979 to 1981 he was a scientist at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] at the CPT (Centre de Physique Theorique) in [[Marseille]]-Luminy. At the same time, he acted in an advisory capacity for [[Aérospatiale]] and the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|French Atomic Energy Commission]]. From 1981 to 1982 he was Einstein Professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=C.V.|website=Alain Rouet homepage (alain-rouet.com)|url=http://www.alain-rouet.com/index.php?page=cv}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Alain Rouet|website=Institute for Advanced Studies|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/alain-rouet}}</ref> He then moved into industry and from 1983 to 1986 was the technical director of a [[Thomson Group]] company ''Vidéolor'', which developed television tubes.<ref name=CV/>

From 1986 to 2017 he was involved in the creation and development of Science & Tec, a kind of scientific [[think tank]] that provided scientific consulting services for industry. Clients included [[AREVA]], [[Bosch (company)|Bosch]], [[European Aeronautic Defense and Space Company|EADS]], and [[TotalEnergies]]. Rouet was involved in the creation and support of Science & Tec subsidiaries in Germany and Italy. From 1996 to 2003 he created and developed Quantaflow, a company that designed, manufactured, and sold an innovative system of software and hardware that counted people at places like shopping centers and airports. The Quantaflow system provided distributed architecture and web services to managers and employees for analysis and certification of customer visits.<ref name=CV/><ref>{{cite web|title=Our Company|website=Quantaflow (quantaflow.com)|url=https://www.quantaflow.com/en/our-company/}}</ref>

Rouet is known for his collaborative development in the mid-1970s with [[Raymond Stora]] and [[Carlo Becchi]] of the [[BRST formalism]]<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Becchi, C.|author2=Rouet, A.|author3=Stora, R.|title=Renormalization of gauge theories|journal=Annals of Physics|date=June 1976|volume=98|issue=2|pages=287–321|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(76)90156-1|bibcode = 1976AnPhy..98..287B |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/RCP25_1975__22__A10_0/}}</ref> (independently done by [[Igor Tyutin]]). The formalism is a method for quantizing a field theory with a [[gauge symmetry]]. In addition to [[quantum field theory]], Rouet also did research on [[dynamical system]]s.<ref name=CV/>

He received, jointly with Stora, Becchi, and Tyutin, the 2009 [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2009 Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics Recipient: Alain Rouet|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Rouet&first_nm=Alain&year=2009}}</ref>
